Modernist composer John Cage wrote -- quite frankly -- weird pieces for the sake of being weird. Cage is the father of chance music, also called aleatoric music or indeterminacy, in which compositions are created at random, quite literally from rolling dice. Works are left up to the musician or audience to interpret and create meaning. This piece was meant to have the ambient sounds going on during the silence become the work.
